housing: Pendle's towns grew on cotton weaving, so Nelson, Colne, Brierfield and Barnoldswick are filled with rows of Victorian stone and brick terraces, many of them privately rented and some long-term empty. House prices are among the lowest in Lancashire. The council has used selective licensing in the past in parts of Nelson, Brierfield and Colne. Around Pendle Hill and towards the Dales the villages have stone cottages and farmhouses, often off the gas grid.
checkinTips: Stone terraces in Nelson, Colne and Brierfield: photograph damp at the base of walls, cellar heads and mould in back bedrooms.
Back yards and back streets behind terraced rows: record the yard gate, walls, outside toilet if any and where the bins are kept.
Hillside terraces in Colne: photograph steps, retaining walls, gutters and any damp in rooms built into the slope.
Stone cottages in Trawden and the Pendle Hill villages: photograph stoves, chimneys, damp in thick walls and any oil tank or LPG supply with the fuel level.
Older terraces with original features: record sash or replacement windows, fireplaces and any gas fires.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Pendle Borough Council's housing standards team.
